svg.aria-label: What's in the box. In the box, one routing point per provider with no model reading every event: the GitHub service flow, which takes events by webhook push or by polling on each user's own schedule rows, at each subscription's own cadence and no more often than every 5 minutes, into one normalized event, the service action's input over WebhookInboundEvent; subscriptions, a user-scoped collection written only by the subscribe and unsubscribe tools, which config-declared subscriptions seed through, ended per ER-7, with a coding task subscribed to its PR when the PR opens; the screen chain, a sequencer that runs config screens first, the sender check among them and failing closed, then the app's custom screen blocks, then one Jev evaluator call per event, and no generator; delivery through sendMessage's exempt path with a server-set source label, an id per object, version and session, and a cap per subscription; work modes on the coordinator for unmatched kinds, off, observe or auto; and routines, one name, list and tool set for every standing instruction that fires as its owner, on a clock or on an event, over the schedule rows and subscription rows, with no new store. Composed in by the app: its custom screen blocks, its list of unmatched kinds to forward, the coordinator's work mode, one key beside routing, and the routines it declares in config. Replaced in one line: sessionId on a GitHub webhook binding becomes a subscription on the thread key, and the GitHub guide's routing code becomes a subscribe call; other providers keep sessionId, as Q5 decided; and recurring work and subscriptions, two lists and two tool sets, become one list of routines, with subscription the name of the event trigger. Not built, below a fence: a generator in routing, the service flow filing tasks, a second messaging API or a roster worker, push to screens which is FIX-2367's, cross-provider identity, a Slack flow, as Q4 decided, long-term memory or a watchdog.
